title: ～代わりに — instead of ～, in return for ～
summary: Has two uses: doing or using something else in place of the original, and giving something in return for a favor or benefit. Nouns take の; verbs and adjectives take the plain form.

patterns.form: V普通形／Aい／Aなだ→な＋代わりに

body.p: 'A のかわりに B' means doing or using B instead of A. 父の代わりに会議に出る means attending the meeting because your father cannot.
～してくれた代わりに、～する expresses giving something back for a favor. It can also balance a good point against a bad one: 安い代わりに、味はよくない (cheap, but the taste suffers).

examples.ja: 父（ちち）の代（か）わりに私（わたし）が会議（かいぎ）に出（で）ます。
examples.romaji: Chichi no kawari ni watashi ga kaigi ni demasu.
examples.tr: I'll attend the meeting instead of my father.

examples.ja: エレベーターの代（か）わりに階段（かいだん）を使（つか）った。
examples.romaji: Erebētā no kawari ni kaidan o tsukatta.
examples.tr: I used the stairs instead of the elevator.

examples.ja: 手伝（てつだ）ってくれた代（か）わりに、昼食（ちゅうしょく）をごちそうした。
examples.romaji: Tetsudatte kureta kawari ni, chūshoku o gochisō shita.
examples.tr: In return for helping me, I treated them to lunch.

pitfalls: Nouns need の: 父の代わりに, not 父代わりに.
Tell the two meanings apart by context: substitution or return.
